answer: One concrete defense is bonding. Every agent identity locks a stake that gets slashed if its attestations are later shown to be coordinated or fake, so spinning up thousands of sybil agents costs real capital. A kernel level check ties each signing key to one bonded account, and a public beacon of penalties lets peers see who was slashed at dawn of each epoch. New identities also face slow reputation ramps through verified work, which makes a sybil swarm expensive to build and slow to pay off.
